caption: Figure 12.1: Upstream CuPy sparse mode (use_gpu=True, fused=False) versus matrix-free fused CUDA kernels and CUDA Graphs (use_gpu=True, fused=True). Top: with CPML, TF/SF, dispersive ADE, tensor averaging, and monitors active, Python dispatch launches up to ~500 small CuPy kernels per step, leaving the GPU at ~11% utilization (7.3 ms/step launch floor on 3D CPML). Bottom: wakis/gpu_fused.py fuses the stencil updates, boundaries, sources, monitors, and transposed adjoint step into custom CUDA RawKernels replayed 64 steps at a time via a FusedLoop CUDA Graph, raising GPU utilization to 93% (45–49× speedup on the invrs full ceviche waveguide bend).
visual_intent:
Textbook-quality scientific schematic for a computational electromagnetics user manual. Flat vector style on a white background, high contrast, thin dark outlines, generous whitespace, sans-serif labels. Colour code used in every figure: primary grid G, interior domains, and fused GPU items in blue; dual grid G-tilde, ghost halos, and standard CuPy items in orange; exact/topological/CPU baseline items in dark grey; high-utilization/speedup items in green; launch-overhead bottlenecks or idle gaps in red. Colourblind-safe. Every label must be spelled exactly as listed in this brief; mathematical symbols must be typeset correctly (hats, tildes, subscripts, transposes). Do not add any number, value, equation, software name, product name, logo, watermark or title that is not listed in this brief. Prefer fewer, larger labels over many small ones. No 3D photorealism, no cartoon characters, no hand-drawn or xkcd style.

Two horizontal execution-pipeline strips stacked vertically. TOP STRIP headed in red/orange '1. Upstream CuPy Sparse Mode (use_gpu=True, fused=False)': On the left, a box 'CSR curl matrices (cupyx.scipy.sparse.csr_matrix) + Python per-step dispatch'. To the right, a GPU timeline bar showing a long train of tiny narrow orange blocks separated by wide red idle gaps, labelled 'up to ~500 small CuPy kernel launches / step (curl, CPML, TF/SF, ADE, tensor, monitors)'. On the far right, a red summary badge: '~11% GPU utilization, 7.3 ms/step launch floor on 3D CPML; invrs bend fwd+adj: 753 s'. BOTTOM STRIP headed in blue/green '2. Matrix-Free Fused CUDA Kernels + CUDA Graphs (use_gpu=True, fused=True, wakis/gpu_fused.py)': On the left, a blue box listing the fused modules: 'leapfrog step + CPML + sources + DFT/flux/mode monitors + TF/SF + tensor averaging + dispersive ADE + exact transposed adjoint'. In the centre, a wide green bracket labelled 'FusedLoop CUDA Graph: replayed 64 steps at a time' enclosing tightly packed solid blue kernel blocks ('custom CUDA RawKernels: zero CSR index traffic, zero Python launch gap'). On the far right, a green summary badge: '93% GPU utilization; invrs bend fwd+adj: 15–17 s (45–49× speedup); matches CuPy to ≤ 10⁻¹¹, adjoint dot-product < 10⁻¹²'.

Above or below this timeline, a label reads: "up to ~500 small CuPy kernel launches / step (curl, CPML, TF/SF, ADE, tensor, monitors)".
*   **Right Side (Metrics):** A red summary badge or callout box containing the performance metrics: "~11% GPU utilization, 7.3 ms/step launch floor on 3D CPML; invrs bend fwd+adj: 753 s".

**Bottom Strip: Matrix-Free Fused CUDA Kernels**
*   **Heading:** Positioned at the top left of this strip in blue/green text: "2. Matrix-Free Fused CUDA Kernels + CUDA Graphs (`use_gpu=True, fused=True, wakis/gpu_fused.py`)".
*   **Left Side (Setup):** A blue rectangular box listing the consolidated fused modules: "leapfrog step + CPML + sources + DFT/flux/mode monitors + TF/SF + tensor averaging + dispersive ADE + exact transposed adjoint".
*   **Center (Timeline):** A horizontal GPU execution timeline depicting high efficiency. *   No 3D photorealism, hand-drawn elements, cartoon characters, shadows, or gradients.
